description: A cat armored in noon-light. Its golden scales drink the desert sun and pay it back in blinding flashes.
lore: More people have followed this cat than any other animal in Nangijala, and every one of them was following something it has not got. The plates look like gold, and gold is [[lore/the_gold_agreement|the one thing everybody here agrees about]], so a person who has seen gold is certain about it in a way they are almost never certain about anything. In shade the cat is the colour of ordinary sand. Nothing comes off it. It is a cat.

The flash is not a display, it is the entire defence. At noon it turns broadside, the plates take the sun and hand it back, and whoever is behind it loses their eyes for a count of ten, which is all it needs and all it ever uses. Early and late it hides instead, and hides well, because sand is what it actually is. The ones who get close go at dawn and stop expecting gold.

There was a man who followed one for eleven years. He gave up his work for it, walked out of two fires' rotas to do it, and got near enough four times to watch the plates dull over in shadow, which should have ended the business and did not. Asked what he meant to do if he ever caught the animal, he said he had stopped thinking about that part around year three. He was not a fool by then and he was not greedy. He had somewhere to be every morning, in a country where you can wake up and find you have nothing to do for the next four hundred years, and he had decided that was the better half of the bargain.
gm_notes: Wires the gold chapter into an entity at last, and does it by making the gold false: the scales are noon-light, the certainty is imported from the one substance that never drifts. The follower is a free-standing leaf about the setting's real question (what do you do with forever) and costs two lapsed rota shifts, so he is not simply sympathetic. No scale has ever come off; keep it that way if a junk item is ever bound here.
